evidence.support_text: Applications of 10% TBU in DMP to guinea-pig skin produced moderate to no irritation and no skin sensitization occurred.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical and intra-dermal administration in guinea pigs
evidence.support_text: PGE was positive in skin sensitization tests in guinea pigs after topical and intra-dermal administration (Kohn and Kay, 1966; Weil et al., 1963; Zschunke and Behrbohm, 1965; Betso et al., 1986).

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test (epicutaneous application)
evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.1 ml of 0.01 M BeF₂ in methyl cellulose wetting agent (MCWT) applied percutaneously to guinea pigs for skin tests 1-4; scoring based on reaction scale.
evidence.support_text: In Table VII, group 1 (standard controls) received no pretreatment and were skin-tested with 0.1 ml of 0.01 M BeF₂ in MCWT. The mean percentage of responders across skin tests 2, 3, and 4 was 95% with a mean score of 4.65, indicating that BeF₂ induces skin sensitization upon topical application.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test (induction and challenge)
evidence.experimental_conditions: 50% Synthetic Beeswax in distilled water with 1% carboxymethyl cellulose and 0.2% Polysorbate 80, applied to clipped backs of guinea pigs 3 consecutive days/week for 3 weeks, one challenge at 14 days after last application. First application 0.5 ml, remaining nine 0.1 ml per application.
evidence.support_text: Fifty percent Synthetic Beeswax (in distilled water) with 1% carboxymethyl cellulose and 0.2% Polysorbate 80 was applied to the clipped backs of guinea pigs for 3 consecutive days/week for 3 weeks with one application in the fourth week. Challenge occurred at 14 days after the last application. The scores were 0.16/4.0 (erythema) and 0.05/4.0 (edema). The investigators concluded that the test material had no potential for irritation or sensitization.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig skin sensitization test (intracutaneous and topical application)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Pretreatment with 1% D₄ in paraffin oil by intracutaneous and closed dermal topical application of neat D₄ for 48 h; challenge reaction with undiluted and 10% test substance in paraffin oil by occluded patch test on day 14 after exposure
evidence.support_text: A skin sensitization test in guinea pigs after pretreatment to 1% D₄ in paraffin oil by intracutaneous and closed dermal topical application of neat D₄ for 48 h, with challenge reaction using undiluted and 10% test substance in paraffin oil by occluded patch test on day 14 after exposure, indicated that D₄ is not a sensitizer at concentrations up to 10% D₄ in paraffin oil, as well as neat D₄. SCCS (2010) and REACH (2011) also concluded that D₄ is not a skin sensitizer.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig skin sensitization test (intravenous injection then skin testing)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Intravenous injection of beryllium (19.15 µg Be per kg), skin testing 15 days later with BeF₂ topical application; guinea pig model.
evidence.support_text: Injection of beryllium (19.15 µg per kg) by the IV route had no sensitising effect as shown by skin testing 15 days later, and did not modify significantly further active sensitisation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application; challenge dose; observation at 24, 48, and 72 h after dressing removal; scoring per ISO 10993-10:2010. Control and treated areas both scored 0.
evidence.support_text: The present study evaluated the delayed immunological response of dextran stabilized iron oxide nanoparticles (DINP) in guinea pigs. The appearance of the challenge skin sites of both test and control guinea pigs was observed at 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h after removal of dressings and patches after the challenge dose. The specific clinical manifestations/skin reactions were scored and the numerical grading was recorded as per ISO 10993-10:2010 (E). The topically exposed DINP did not induce any skin irritation after a challenge dose. The skin irritation scores of DINP treated and control areas were designated as '0', indicating no sensitization.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test (Magnusson and Kligman scale)
evidence.experimental_conditions: physiological saline extract; challenge patch on shaved skin; readings at 24 h and 48 h; species: guinea pig; sex: female; n=10
evidence.support_text: In Table, for FLG-C-NR latex thin film, group G2 (physiological saline extract, 10 female guinea pigs) showed a Magnusson and Kligman score of 0 at both the control (C) and test (T) sites at both 24 h and 48 h after removal of the challenge patch, indicating no skin sensitization reaction.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig skin sensitization test (maximizing allergic contact dermatitis)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig test, technique from Watson, Murphy & Turner (1983) that maximizes skin sensitization
evidence.support_text: Watson, Murphy & Turner (1983) employed a technique used to test compounds for their potential for producing allergic contact dermatitis and that also maximizes the degree of skin sensitization of guinea pigs. Sensitivity was greatly increased by THC and cannabinol, but less so with other cannabinoids.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig skin sensitization test (OECD guideline)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig, highest concentration, 48 h observation
evidence.support_text: In summary, MPD was negative in a GLP, OECD Guideline Guinea pig skin sensitization test. Only 1/20 animals reacted slightly to the highest concentration after 48 h.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test (OECD SIDS)
evidence.experimental_conditions: neat TPA; guinea pig; details not specified
evidence.support_text: Neat TPA was not a guinea pig skin sensitizer as reported in OECD SIDS (2001a).

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test (percutaneous application of BeF₂)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Percutaneous application of BeF₂ in MCWT to male guinea-pigs; skin test after 7 days; mean score of skin tests 2-4 excluding first non-specific response; no pre-treatment.
evidence.support_text: In the control group (no pre-treatment), 100% of guinea pigs gave positive skin responses after percutaneous application of BeF₂, with a mean score of 5.6 across skin tests 2, 3, and 4 (Table IV). The paper states that beryllium fluoride sensitises guinea pigs, as shown by the positive skin reactions in all controls.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig skin sensitization test (topical application and skin testing)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application of BeF₂ in MCWT, dose 140 µg per test (350 µg Be per kg), skin testing 15 days later, repeated skin paintings for active sensitization; guinea pig model.
evidence.support_text: Topical application of BeF₂ (140 µg per skin test, 350 µg Be per kg) to guinea pigs elicited positive skin sensitization responses, as shown by 10/10 animals responding in the second skin test with a mean score of 4.30 (control group, no pre-treatment).

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig skin sensitization test (topical application with pre-treatment)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application of 140 µg beryllium as BeF2; guinea-pigs from source 1 pre-treated by injection of 5 µg beryllium (as fluoride)/kg 25 and 18 days before the first skin test; three applications.
evidence.support_text: In the table, BeF2-treated guinea-pigs pre-treated by injection of 5 µg beryllium (as fluoride) per kg showed 0/4, 2/4, and 1/4 positive responses in the three skin tests, with mean scores of 0, 1.5, and 1.5 respectively.

evidence.assay_type: Guinea pig skin sensitization test (topical application)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Topical application of 140 µg beryllium as BeSO4; guinea-pigs from source 1; three applications.
evidence.support_text: BeSO4 gave 30% positive animals after three applications in the same source 1 guinea-pigs, compared to 60% for BeF2.

evidence.experimental_conditions: concentration of PAA as 0.02% impurity in TFL; test system: guinea pig (likely Magnusson & Kligman and Buehler test)
evidence.support_text: This level of PAA (residual PAA in pre-technical TFL at 0.02%) was not sufficient to induce skin sensitization in the same test (likely guinea pig maximization test) as well as in the Buehler test system.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test after pre-treatment with Be citrate IP
evidence.experimental_conditions: Pre-treatment with Be citrate 19.15 µg Be/kg IP (single injection 15 days before first skin test). Challenged percutaneously with BeF₂.
evidence.support_text: Guinea-pigs pre-treated with 19.15 µg Be/kg as beryllium citrate IP had 54% responders with a mean score of 0.8 across skin tests 2-4 (Table IV). The paper notes that beryllium citrate induced a significant degree of tolerance (paragraph 36).

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test after pre-treatment with Be phosphate IP
evidence.experimental_conditions: Pre-treatment with Be phosphate 19.15 µg Be/kg IP (single injection 15 days before first skin test). Challenged percutaneously with BeF₂.
evidence.support_text: Guinea-pigs pre-treated with 19.15 µg Be/kg as beryllium phosphate IP had 67% responders with a mean score of 2.1 across skin tests 2-4 (Table IV). The paper states that beryllium phosphate did not induce a significant degree of tolerance at the 1% level (Table IV, paragraph 36).

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test after pre-treatment with BeF₂ IP
evidence.experimental_conditions: Pre-treatment with BeF₂ 10.8 µg/kg IP (single injection 15 days before first skin test). Challenged percutaneously with BeF₂.
evidence.support_text: Guinea-pigs pre-treated intraperitoneally with 10.8 µg Be/kg as BeF₂ 15 days before the first skin test had 60% responders (4/5 by the third test) with a mean score of 1.1 across skin tests 2-4 (Table IV). This indicates immune tolerance was induced.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test after pre-treatment with BeF₂ IP
evidence.experimental_conditions: Pre-treatment with BeF₂ 19.15 µg/kg IP (single injection 15 days before first skin test). Challenged percutaneously with BeF₂.
evidence.support_text: Guinea-pigs pre-treated IP with 19.15 µg Be/kg as BeF₂ had only 40% responders (positive skin reactions) with a mean score of 1.6 across skin tests 2-4 (Table IV), demonstrating a marked reduction in sensitization due to immune tolerance.

evidence.assay_type: guinea pig skin sensitization test after pre-treatment with BeF₂ IV
evidence.experimental_conditions: Pre-treatment with BeF₂ 19.15 µg/kg IV (single injection 15 days before first skin test). Challenged percutaneously with BeF₂.
evidence.support_text: Guinea-pigs pre-treated intravenously with 19.15 µg Be/kg as BeF₂ had 56% responders with a mean score of 3.7 across skin tests 2-4 (Table IV). The paper states that the same dose given IV does not modify the immunological status significantly (paragraph 40).

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig, 12.5 µg/50 mg difluprednate ointment, 6-hour closed patch on flank, observation 24 and 48 h after patch removal
evidence.support_text: In a topical antigenicity test, guinea pigs were sensitized with difluprednate ointment and challenged with 12.5 µg/50 mg difluprednate ointment by 6-hour closed patch on the flank. Observation at 24 and 48 h after patch removal showed no contact allergic reaction (score 0) at any site.
In the guinea-pig maximization test, Zeolithe A showed no evidence of skin-sensitizing properties.

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig; 0.5 ml undiluted Trimethylolpropane Trimethacrylate; Webril pad occluded with elastoplast for 5 hours; challenge at 2 weeks; scoring at 24 and 49 hours
evidence.support_text: Trimethylolpropane Trimethacrylate (0.5 ml) was applied undiluted for 5 hours to a Webril pad which was occluded with elastoplast. Two weeks later, a challenge was done using Trimethylolpropane Trimethacrylate at the insult and virgin site for 5 hours. Irritation was scored at 24 and 49 hours. No irritation was noted at any time. Trimethylolpropane Trimethacrylate was not considered a sensitizer.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Skin samples from 6 of 10 guinea pigs from the second group (10 daily injections of 0.5% Quaternium-15) were evaluated microscopically after challenge.
evidence.support_text: Skin samples were evaluated microscopically from 6 of 10 animals in the second group; no microscopic indication of contact sensitization was observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig; intradermal injection of 0.2 ml of 2 mg/ml potassium dichromate in saline; skin biopsy at 48 h; 400× magnification
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig model (Groups A, B, C; n=3/group), Group B received an intradermal injection of 0.2 ml of 2 mg/ml Cr(VI) (potassium dichromate) in saline. Immunohistochemistry at 48 hours showed that the Cr(VI)-exposed group (Group B) induced expression of IL-1α (arrow) in the epidermis (400×), while the control group (saline) showed no staining.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig; intradermal injection of 0.2 ml of 2 mg/ml potassium dichromate in saline; skin biopsy at 48 h; 400× magnification
evidence.support_text: In a guinea pig model (Groups A, B, C; n=3/group), Group B received an intradermal injection of 0.2 ml of 2 mg/ml Cr(VI) (potassium dichromate) in saline. Immunohistochemistry at 48 hours showed that the Cr(VI)-exposed group (Group B) induced expression of TNF-α (arrow) in the epidermis (400×), while the control group (saline) showed no staining.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% triclosan in 5% polyethylene glycol, 0.1 ml intradermal injection, 3 times/week for 10 injections, challenge 2 weeks later
evidence.support_text: Intradermal injection of 0.1 ml of 1% triclosan in 5% polyethylene glycol to guinea pigs three times per week for a total of 10 injections followed by a challenge injection 2 weeks later resulted in no consistent triclosan-related sensitization (negative).

evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig, intradermal injection, one week after four-week inhalation exposure
evidence.support_text: An intradermal skin test was also performed on 50% of the animals one week after the inhalation challenge, and there was no evidence of skin sensitisation either (Gerlach et al., 1989).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig (female); intratracheal instillation of 0.6% TDI (total dose 0.3 mg per animal) on day 1; challenge on day 15 with 0.4 ml of 1% TDI in liquid paraffin by closed patch for 6 h; scored 24 and 48 h post-challenge; positive defined as score ≥1 at either time.
evidence.support_text: Four of the five animals exhibited skin sensitivity at 24 and 48 h post-challenge, yielding a sensitization rate of 80%. One animal gave no reaction at either time period.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Lymph node cells from guinea pigs sensitized to BP via footpad with CFA; test antigen concentration not specified; optimal concentration used.
evidence.support_text: Table II shows that BP-skin protein (isocyanate conjugate) from FP-CFA-sensitized guinea pigs gave a mean stimulation index of 1.49 ± 0.01 in 4 of 8 animals tested, indicating significant lymphocyte transformation.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Test antigen: BP-skin protein isocyanate conjugate; route of sensitization: footpad (FP) with complete Freund's adjuvant (CFA); lymph node cells from BP-sensitized guinea pigs.
evidence.support_text: In lymphocyte transformation tests of lymph node cells from BP-sensitized guinea pigs, the BP-skin protein isocyanate conjugate administered via footpad (FP) with CFA gave a mean stimulation index of 1.49 ± 0.01 for positive tests, with 4 out of 8 animals positive.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Antigen concentration 50–200 µg/ml; peritoneal exudate cells from guinea pigs sensitized to BP in FCA via footpad.
evidence.support_text: Table I shows that BP-skin protein III (isocyanate conjugate) gave a migration index of 82.0 (mean of positive tests) in 1 of 6 animals tested, indicating significant migration inhibition.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Antigen concentration 50–200 µg/ml; peritoneal exudate cells from guinea pigs sensitized to BP in FCA via footpad.
evidence.support_text: Table I shows that BP-skin protein IV (isocyanate conjugate) gave a mean migration index of 84.0 ± 2.9 (mean ± SEM) in 2 of 2 animals tested, indicating significant migration inhibition.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs; test substance purity 74.33%; method per OECD Guideline 406
evidence.support_text: The sensitisation potential of GLDA-Na4 (74.33%) was assessed in a Magnusson & Kligman maximisation test, following OECD Guideline 406. None of the guinea pigs exposed to GLDA-Na4 showed positive skin responses. GLDA-Na4 is not considered as a skin sensitiser.

evidence.support_text: o-CGE produced skin sensitization in 16 of 20 guinea pigs tested using the Magnusson and Kligman maximization test (Ullmann et al., 1991).

evidence.support_text: GENA was a severe skin sensitizer in guinea pigs when tested according to the Magnusson and Kligman maximization test (Clark and Coombs, 1977).

evidence.support_text: LAE did not elicit a skin sensitization response in guinea pigs following induction and challenge in the Magnusson and Kligman Test. The study concluded that neither LAE nor Mirenat-N demonstrates skin sensitization in this test.
